Distributions of EV arrival time and SOC Key power profiles are presented in Figure 21, along with the BESS SOC. The grid power profile demonstrates that the SCM controller can successfully enforce a power ceiling, ensuring good performance while avoiding costly distribution and interconnection upgrades. The BESS power profile demonstrates how the algorithm charges the battery (negative power values) when solar generation peaks and discharges it when solar generation is low and EVSE and building loads are high, successfully shaving the peak load. The building load, not shown in the graph, stays relatively constant around 1 MW throughout the day. Figure 21. The distribution of EV charging times is shown in Figure 22, which indicates that the majority of charging sessions are completed within 15–30 minutes. This result is a combination of the EV arrival SOC and assigned EVSE power level; EVs with lower SOC are assigned to high-speed chargers, while EVs with higher SOC are assigned to low-speed chargers, balancing out the charging time distribution. Figure 22. Distributions of EV charging time For the hardware portion of the test, the GMC Hummer EV started charging with an SOC of 45% and was connected to the Delta DC Wallbox EVSE charger with a rated capacity of 25 kW. The Hyundai Ioniq 5 EV started charging with an SOC of 56% and was connected to the Bosch EV3000 EVSE charger with a rated capacity of 30 kW. Each vehicle was charged until it reached 80% SOC. The power and SOC profiles are shown in Figure 23, which indicates that the Ioniq achieves its desired SOC much faster than the Hummer even when charging at a slightly lower power level, as expected due to the battery size difference. Power profiles were observed to remain mostly constant, as expected from low-power DC fast chargers, requiring a low level of intervention or curtailment by the SCM controller. 33 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. Power and SOC measurements for the PHIL hardware test Overall, the performance of the Gold SCM framework agrees with the simulation results, demonstrating that a similar control structure can be deployed in practice. Lab tests confirm that the SCM can keep the total grid power below the limit (2 MW) by utilizing the energy storage and controlling the charging power of the EVSE, using a combination of feedback and heuristic rules. The framework was also able to handle real EV and EVSE hardware without any adverse effects.
